description: Reference answer for the NovaCart demo estate. API Galaxy's AI enrichment pass is scored against this file: the domains, business entities, capabilities and relationships below are what a correct semantic read of the seven specs should produce.

domains.name: Customer
domains.description: Owns shopper identity, contact details, loyalty standing and the saved address book.

domains.name: Catalog
domains.description: Owns the published product assortment, the merchandising category tree and keyword search.

domains.name: Cart
domains.description: Owns the shopper's in-progress basket and the handover point into checkout.

domains.name: Order
domains.description: Owns the order book: the immutable commercial contract created when a basket is accepted.

domains.name: Payment
domains.description: Owns money movement against an order, from authorization hold through capture and refunds.

domains.name: Inventory
domains.description: Owns warehouse stock positions and the soft-reservation ledger that protects them.

domains.name: Shipping
domains.description: Owns carrier bookings, tracking numbers and the parcel scan history shown to shoppers.

business_entities.name: Customer
business_entities.description: A person with a NovaCart account. The single most aliased concept in the estate: it changes name at every service boundary on the checkout path.

business_entities.name: Address
business_entities.description: A postal location a parcel can be sent to. Customer models it as a first-class schema; Order copies it inline onto the order; Shipping keeps its own structurally identical destination object with no declared link.

business_entities.name: Product
business_entities.description: A merchandised article offered for sale, identified by the catalogue surrogate key product_id.

business_entities.name: Stock Keeping Unit
business_entities.description: The physical article that is actually picked, packed and counted. The only identifier shared verbatim by Catalog, Cart, Order and Inventory.

business_entities.name: Cart
business_entities.description: A mutable working basket held between browsing and ordering, owned by exactly one customer.

business_entities.name: Order
business_entities.description: The frozen commercial contract created when a basket is accepted. Payment, Inventory and Shipping all attach to it by order_id.

business_entities.name: Payment
business_entities.description: The money taken for one order, tracked from authorization hold through capture and refunds.

business_entities.name: Monetary Amount
business_entities.description: A currency-denominated value. Modelled inconsistently across the estate: a JSON number in Cart and Order, an exact decimal string in Payment.

business_entities.name: Inventory Reservation
business_entities.description: A short-lived soft hold on stock taken for an order, which either commits to a pick or expires.

business_entities.name: Shipment
business_entities.description: A parcel booked with a carrier against an order, followed by a stream of tracking scans.

capabilities.name: Manage Shopper Identity
capabilities.description: Register shoppers, amend their profiles and serve their saved addresses to the rest of the estate.

capabilities.name: Discover Products
capabilities.description: Let a shopper browse, search and inspect the published assortment before they commit to buying.

capabilities.name: Build a Basket
capabilities.description: Accumulate intended purchases at a stable price and keep a running subtotal until checkout.

capabilities.name: Check Out
capabilities.description: Turn a basket into a binding order by validating the shopper, holding stock and authorizing money, all in one gated step.

capabilities.name: Manage Orders
capabilities.description: Read, list and cancel orders across the shopper portal and the back-office support console.

capabilities.name: Take Payment
capabilities.description: Hold, settle and return money against an order while keeping an auditable payment record.

capabilities.name: Protect Stock
capabilities.description: Report what is on hand and stop two shoppers from buying the same last unit, using expiring soft holds.

capabilities.name: Deliver Parcels
capabilities.description: Book carriers, issue tracking numbers and narrate a parcel's journey until it is delivered.

relationships.reason: Validates the customer exists and is not blocked before the order is accepted.
Re-reads the basket so the order freezes the exact lines and subtotal the shopper saw.
Holds stock for every SKU on the basket so the order cannot be placed against thin air.
Authorizes the payment instrument for the order total before the order is written.
Delegates basket-to-order conversion to the Order domain and returns the resulting order.
Reads the order lines and delivery destination that the parcel must be booked against.
Turns the soft stock hold into a firm allocation so the warehouse can pick the goods.
Confirms the order is still live and its lines still match the held quantities.
Confirms the order is still live and the capture amount does not exceed the order total.
Structurally and semantically identical postal address with no shared schema, no $ref and no declared dependency. Only a semantic reader can join these two.
The order copies the shopper's saved address inline at placement time rather than referencing the Customer schema.
The Order domain's legacy name for the canonical shopper identifier.
The Payment domain's own name for the canonical shopper identifier.
Cart uses the canonical name verbatim, which is what makes the Order and Payment renames visible as drift.
The same money value carried as a decimal string on one side of the boundary and a JSON number on the other.

notes.explicit_vs_inferable: Explicit relationships are the nine x-api-galaxy-depends-on edges declared in the specs and should be recovered by static parsing alone. Inferable relationships carry kind 'inferable' and exist only in the prose and field naming; recovering them is the job of the AI enrichment pass and is what this file scores.
notes.cycle: order-api:placeOrder to inventory-api:reserveInventory combined with inventory-api:commitReservation to order-api:getOrder forms the intended Order and Inventory cycle.
